text: Over the next twenty-two videos, you're going to answer one real business question for a fictional specialty retailer, Northfield Retail Co.: are we losing customers, and why?

You'll build a T-SQL query that defines what that question even means in data, a Power BI dashboard, a Python check Power BI can't do alone, a Tableau version for a field team, and an Excel reconciliation that catches mistakes early.
But none of that starts this video. This video is the one meeting that decides whether everything after it is useful — or wasted effort.
The Sales Director is about to tell you she thinks they're losing customers. That sounds simple. It isn't a metric — it has no agreed time window, no agreed definition of 'lost.'

Different reasonable definitions of churn — ninety days inactive versus one-eighty, versus an actual cancellation — produce wildly different numbers from the exact same table. Pick one without agreement, and you're the one blamed when finance's number doesn't match yours.

Watch how the conversation actually goes: she has a feeling about the Southeast region, not hard numbers — and she doesn't actually know the right churn window either. That's not a gap to quietly fill in yourself. It's a decision to make together.
What you'll leave with is an operational definition precise enough that two different analysts, given the same data, compute the same number — confirmed in writing before a single query gets written.
That's the step that decides whether the dashboard you eventually ship gets trusted, or challenged. Let's sit in on the meeting.
